sentences.text: The holotype specimen — the specific fossil the species is based on — includes shoulder elements, five back vertebrae, three tail vertebrae, pubic bones, ischia, and a left femur.
A unique trait of Jiangshanosaurus is that in specific tail vertebrae, ridges from the neural spine are placed inside the front articulation processes rather than touching them.
The shoulder structure of Jiangshanosaurus is very similar to that of Alamosaurus.
A sauropod skeleton was excavated in 1977 and 1978 from the Jinhua Formation in Lixian Village, Zhejiang province, China.
The species Jiangshanosaurus lixianensis was formally described by Tang Feng and colleagues in 2001.
A 2019 study placed Jiangshanosaurus in the Somphospondyli in a basal position outside the Titanosauria.
While initially considered an advanced Titanosaur, recent studies suggest Jiangshanosaurus lies outside the Lithostrotia.
Jiangshanosaurus was a herbivorous sauropod that lived in China between 92 and 88 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
Some sources suggest Jiangshanosaurus lived approximately 105 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Middle Cretaceous in Asia.
The fossil record indicates Jiangshanosaurus lived from the Cenomanian to the Turonian stages, between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago.
